summary:
Radar for 2026-10-22, GLP-1 focus. Four topics have something new today:
(1) Retatrutide for sleep apnea. Full Phase 3 results (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA) appeared in NEJM around Oct 20 and were presented at Sleep Europe 2026. MedPage Today covered them on Oct 21. That is still inside the 48-hour window for a Lane C first explainer, and very few creators have covered it yet.
(2) CBS News published an Oct 21 investigation where it bought and lab-tested products sold as 'Reta' (retatrutide). This is the next step in our strongest lane (Lane B, gray-market 'what's confirmed?').
(3) Medicare's $50 GLP-1 Bridge comes up during open enrollment (Oct 15–Dec 7). That makes it a seasonal Lane A search topic with high ad rates.
(4) New research from the American Academy of Ophthalmology meeting on GLP-1s and the eye. It needs careful, non-scary framing.
Main checks: the compounded tirzepatide recall now has fresh facts (Class II, 22 lots, 14 FDA inspection observations). But we already did a recall Short on 10-20, so a long-form is only allowed if it's a broader 'is my GLP-1 legit?' piece. For the MedPage sleep-apnea story, the drug was confirmed as retatrutide through NEJM's own post on X. I couldn't verify the Medscape alcohol story directly; the alcohol evidence rests on the Lancet-family trial and the Addictive Behaviors review. Orforglipron and 'Wegovy pill vs shot' topics have underperformed for us, so they rank lower. One reject: a 'retatrutide reconstitution technical guide' (preparation how-to for an unapproved drug).

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: full Phase 3 results (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and TRIUMPH-2-OSA) published in NEJM about Oct 20, 2026. Adults with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea and obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: Lane C first explainer, series 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded'. Title idea: 'Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found' (54 characters). Cover breathing pauses per hour on each dose versus placebo, how this compares with tirzepatide's approved sleep-apnea use (SURMOUNT-OSA, described as indirect), and the common stomach side effects. Retatrutide is still investigational: say clearly it isn't approved and Lilly plans to file in Q1 2027. Point viewers to a prescriber about approved options or clinical trials. Never cover online sources.
candidates.predicted_peak: 3–10 days (news cycle, then steady search as 'retatrutide' interest stays high)
candidates.why_now: The full paper landed in NEJM about 48 hours ago and MedPage covered it on Oct 21. Retatrutide is our best-performing drug name, and a new named result within 48 h is the EloraTZP pattern (458 views). Creator coverage of the sleep-apnea angle is still thin; most retatrutide videos are about weight loss or bootleg products.

evidence.signal: 'Retatrutide Once Weekly for Treatment of Obstructive Sleep Apnea', two Phase 3 trials, retatrutide versus placebo on the apnea-hypopnea index
Presented at Sleep Europe 2026. Two Phase 3 trials in sleep apnea with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes: greater drops in the apnea-hypopnea index than placebo
Topline: the apnea-hypopnea index fell by up to 36.1 events per hour (60.6%) from a baseline of 58.6. Most common side effects were nausea, diarrhea, constipation and vomiting. Still investigational
'Another Incretin Drug Proves Mettle in Sleep Apnea'

candidates.topic: What CBS News found when it bought and lab-tested products sold as 'retatrutide' (Oct 21, 2026), plus FDA death reports and Lilly lawsuits
candidates.angle: Lane B, series 'What's Actually Confirmed?'. Title idea: 'Retatrutide Online: What a Lab Test Actually Showed (Oct 2026)'. Credit every line with its date: CBS (Oct 21, 2026), Lilly lawsuits (Oct 8, 2026), FDA death reports (CBS, cause not established). Key point: matching a basic lab reference is not the same as being the trial drug, and products bought without a prescriber skip any health check. Never name the clinics, gym or store CBS bought from, and never give prices or how-to. Point to a prescriber about approved options or trials. Shorts must add a new fact, not repeat the Bootleg Reta script.
candidates.why_now: New CBS investigation (Oct 21) syndicated to affiliates. It follows the Penn Reddit-AI study (ScienceDaily, Oct 22) and the Dutch and Australian hospital-admission reports. Gray-market Shorts are our best lane (median 102), and Lane B long-form is owed this week.

evidence.signal: CBS bought 'Reta' online and from a store without speaking to a clinician. A University of Iowa scientist ran the lab analysis
Two deaths reported to the FDA involving bootleg 'Reta'; cause not established
Lilly lawsuits against the illicit market
Illegal retatrutide use rising in the Netherlands

candidates.topic: Does Medicare cover Wegovy or Zepbound? The $50 Medicare GLP-1 Bridge (Jul 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027) during open enrollment
candidates.angle: Lane A search question. Title idea: 'Does Medicare Cover Wegovy or Zepbound? The $50 Bridge Explained'. Cover who qualifies as reported by KFF (Part D enrollment; BMI 27 or higher with a condition such as heart disease or prediabetes; BMI 35 or higher qualifies on its own), which products are covered (Wegovy pill and injection, Zepbound KwikPen, Foundayo), that the copay doesn't rise with the dose, and the questions to bring to your Part D plan and doctor during open enrollment. Every coverage line is credited to CMS or KFF with a date. No telehealth sellers.
candidates.predicted_peak: Now through Dec 7 (end of open enrollment), with another spike in early January
candidates.why_now: Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15–Dec 7, and ABC7 covered the Bridge again on Oct 22. Older US adults searching coverage questions bring high ad rates. Novo's 2027 price cuts and Q3 earnings keep cost news flowing.

evidence.signal: Bridge pilot Jul 1, 2026 to Dec 31, 2027; $50 copay; Wegovy, Zepbound KwikPen and Foundayo; BMI eligibility criteria
'A new Medicare option for weight loss drugs is coming: here's what to know'
Medicare GLP-1 Bridge coverage recirculating during open enrollment

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) side effects: which are common and what helps. Hooked to a new review of GLP-1 stomach symptoms and gut motility (Neurogastroenterol Motil, Oct 2026) and Yahoo's 'feeling awful on your GLP-1?' piece
candidates.angle: Lane A, series 'Life on GLP-1'. Title idea: 'Tirzepatide Side Effects: Which Are Common and What Helps'. Cover how often nausea, diarrhea and constipation happen in the trials, when they tend to ease, the habits guidelines support (smaller meals, stopping when full, fluids, fibre), and the warning signs that mean calling a clinician. Comparison with semaglutide only as a brief, dated note on SURMOUNT-5 (maximum tolerated doses).
keywords: how long do mounjaro side effects last
candidates.predicted_peak: Evergreen; steady search demand all year
candidates.why_now: Playbook Lane A example with proven search demand. The new motility review and Yahoo's piece give it a fresh hook. Stomach side effects is our best Instagram body-effect topic (103 reach). Our snapshots have carried this topic 3 times at momentum 78.

evidence.signal: 'Gastrointestinal Symptom Events and Motility Alterations Associated With GLP-1 Receptor Agonists'
'Feeling awful on your GLP-1? The drug may not be what's making you miserable'

candidates.topic: Semaglutide plus menopausal hormone therapy: linked to more weight loss (about 16% vs 12% at 12 months; retrospective Mayo Clinic cohort in the journal Menopause), plus Novo's results by menopause stage presented at ECO 2026
candidates.angle: Body-effect question for women aged 45–65. Title idea: 'Semaglutide During Menopause: Does Hormone Therapy Change Results?' Keep it observational: 'linked to', not caused by. Say who was studied, and that hormone therapy has its own risks and benefits to discuss with a clinician. Never suggest starting hormone therapy to boost weight loss.
candidates.why_now: MedicalNewsToday (Oct 21) and Bioengineer (Oct 20) picked it up, and MedPage ran 'GLP-1 in Menopause' (Oct 20). Large female 45–65 audience with high ad rates, a body-effect topic that suits Instagram, and few creator videos so far.

evidence.signal: 'Menopause: Hormone therapy plus Wegovy linked to more weight loss'
Weight loss with Wegovy was consistent across menopause stages (STEP UP post hoc analysis, SELECT, real-world data)
Hormone therapy linked to sustained semaglutide weight loss in an observational cohort

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide or tirzepatide affect your eyes? New research from the American Academy of Ophthalmology meeting (Oct 21): in people who already had NAION, a second episode came earlier with GLP-1 exposure (1,440 users vs 20,713 non-users). A separate study looked at age-related macular degeneration
candidates.angle: Calm body-effect explainer, no scare framing. Title idea: 'Semaglutide and Your Eyes: What the Newest Studies Show'. Explain what NAION is, that it's rare, and that this study only included people who had already had NAION and used medical-records data (users had higher HbA1c). Put it alongside the observational data linking tirzepatide to lower diabetic-retinopathy risk. Action: report sudden vision changes promptly and mention eye history to your prescriber. Never say to stop the medicine.
candidates.why_now: New results from the ophthalmology meeting on Oct 21, a Cureus retinal cohort on Oct 20, and a Clin Ophthalmol paper on Oct 12. 'Ozempic eyes' has steady search demand. Eye topics reached 53 on Instagram, but scare framing underperforms (vision loss: 34), so keep it reassuring and precise.

evidence.signal: Early repeat NAION in 69.5% of users vs 52% of non-users; relative risk 2.63; association only
Association between GLP-1 medicines and age-related macular degeneration explored at the AAO meeting
Semaglutide, diabetic retinopathy and NAION in type 2 diabetes: single-centre retrospective cohort

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide make you weaker? Handgrip-strength meta-analysis (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19) plus how much tirzepatide weight loss is muscle (SURMOUNT-1 body-scan substudy)
candidates.angle: Muscle-outcome question, our proven Short frame (101 and 131 views). Title idea for the Short: 'Tirzepatide vs Semaglutide: Does Strength Drop?' Give the measured result first, then guideline-backed protein and resistance training (Nutrients rapid review). No how-to lists in the title. Long-form only as Lane A: 'How Much Weight Loss on Tirzepatide Is Muscle?'
keywords: how much weight loss is muscle mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Fresh meta-analysis (Oct 19), plus the Forbes 'GLP-1 for muscles' story (Oct 21) and the Nutrients review. Muscle questions are a proven Short lane, and we've seen this topic in 2 snapshots.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength after semaglutide
Rapid review of protein intake and resistance training across clinical populations
'Like a GLP-1 for muscles and cartilage?'

candidates.topic: Is my GLP-1 legit? Compounded tirzepatide recall now FDA Class II (Apothecary Pharma; recall started Sep 24, classified Oct 10; 22 lots; 14 FDA inspection observations), plus USA Today's 'check if the pharmacy is legit'
candidates.angle: Lane B long-form framed broadly, not as another recall Short. Title idea: 'Is My Tirzepatide Legit? What the FDA Says to Check'. Explain approved vs compounded vs counterfeit, what a Class II recall means (the FDA's words), and the FDA's own checks for a licensed pharmacy. Credit and date every line, no sellers, no 'switching' advice, and point to a prescriber about approved options. Our recall Short ran 10-20, so any new Short must lead with a new fact (the 14 FDA observations) and run at most once this week.
keywords: how to check online pharmacy legit
candidates.why_now: Wide mainstream coverage Oct 20–21 (USA Today, LA Times, Boston Globe, Fox Business, The Independent, Good Housekeeping). Searches for affected lots peak now. Gray-market is our strongest lane, but the recall itself is crowded and we already did a Short, so the broader 'legit' framing is the differentiator.

evidence.signal: Recall started Sep 24 for 'lack of assurance of sterility'; FDA classified it Class II on Oct 10; FDA warning letter to the same pharmacy in Dec 2025
14 FDA inspection observations at the pharmacy, including research-grade ingredients
'Getting your GLP-1 online? Check if the pharmacy making it is legit'

candidates.topic: How to enjoy Thanksgiving and holiday meals on tirzepatide or semaglutide (UC Davis Health guide, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Lane A, series 'Life on GLP-1'. Title idea: 'Eating Thanksgiving Dinner on Tirzepatide: What Helps'. Cover smaller plates, protein first, eating slowly, going easy on rich and fatty foods that can worsen nausea, and alcohol caution, all credited to clinical sources. Positive, no restriction or guilt messaging. Ask a clinician about blood-sugar management if you have diabetes.
candidates.predicted_peak: Nov 15–28 (publish by early November to rank)
candidates.why_now: Seasonal: US Thanksgiving is Nov 26. UC Davis has already published, so search demand will build over the next 3–5 weeks. Publishing now lets the video rank before the peak.

evidence.signal: 'How to enjoy holiday meals while taking a GLP-1 weight loss medication'
'Started a GLP-1 drug like Ozempic or Mounjaro? Here's what you need to know about nutrition'

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4 and STEP 1 extension regain data, plus new real-world US data on how often people stop semaglutide early and stay on it at 1 year (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A playbook example. Title idea: 'What Happens When You Stop Semaglutide or Tirzepatide?' Cover what the trials measured, regain patterns, why people stop (cost, side effects), and the habits linked to keeping results. End: talk to your prescriber before any change. Never give stopping or tapering instructions.
keywords: what happens when you stop ozempic
how to keep weight off after wegovy
candidates.why_now: Seen in 3 snapshots at momentum 66–70 and a named Lane A example. The new persistence paper adds a fresh fact, and 2027 coverage changes (open enrollment, Novo price cuts) will push stopping questions up.

evidence.signal: Real-world semaglutide initiation behaviours: early discontinuation and 1-year persistence

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide help people drink less? The Lancet-family trial in alcohol use disorder with obesity, the Addictive Behaviors review (Oct 10), Medscape (Oct 21) and the BMJ news story on a US trial testing semaglutide and criminal behaviour
candidates.angle: Early-research pillar, kept precise. Title idea: 'Does Semaglutide Reduce Drinking? What the Trials Show'. Give heavy-drinking days versus placebo, the population studied, and that it isn't approved for alcohol use. Use the BMJ crime trial as a curiosity re-hook only, labelled as a trial that hasn't reported. Point to clinicians for alcohol support.
candidates.why_now: Repeated coverage (Medscape Oct 21, Medical Economics Oct 20, BMJ Oct 20) and seen in 2 earlier snapshots. Strong curiosity, and less crowded than weight-loss topics.

evidence.signal: Review of semaglutide for alcohol use disorder
'US trial will test whether semaglutide can fight crime'
'GLP-1 Drugs Linked to Reduced Alcohol Consumption'

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide vs retatrutide for sleep apnea: approved option vs investigational (SURMOUNT-OSA vs the TRIUMPH sleep-apnea trials, indirect comparison)
candidates.angle: Two-drug Short with tirzepatide named first. Title idea: 'Tirzepatide vs Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What's Confirmed'. Say plainly that there is no head-to-head trial, that tirzepatide is approved for moderate-to-severe sleep apnea with obesity, and that retatrutide is investigational (filing planned Q1 2027). Funnel to the retatrutide sleep-apnea long-form once it's published.
candidates.why_now: Uses the fresh NEJM paper in our second-best Short format (two named drugs, median 88). The Cardiol Rev review of tirzepatide for sleep apnea (Oct 20) and the Cureus review on stepping down sleep-apnea therapy after GLP-1 weight loss add depth.

evidence.signal: 'Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects'
Retatrutide sleep-apnea Phase 3 publication

candidates.topic: Orforglipron (Foundayo) and the heart: ACHIEVE-4 was non-inferior to insulin glargine on major heart events in type 2 diabetes with heart or kidney disease (2,749 adults), plus the EU CHMP opinion of Oct 16 (Commission decision pending)
candidates.angle: Body-effect Short with two named drugs. Title idea: 'Orforglipron vs Insulin Glargine: Heart Safety Results'. Primary result first (hazard ratio 0.84, non-inferiority met). Label the death results as exploratory. Correct population.
candidates.why_now: Clinical Trial Vanguard analysis (Oct 19) and the EU process are moving. Ranked lower because orforglipron Shorts underperform (36–37).

evidence.signal: Foundayo non-inferior to insulin glargine for cardiovascular outcomes in diabetes
ACHIEVE-4: hazard ratio 0.84 for MACE-4; weight −8.8% vs +1.7% at 52 weeks

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what changed for people who moved from injections to the pill (OCTANE retrospective, 194 adults, average 4.1% further loss over 3 months), plus Yahoo's 'who shouldn't switch' (Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Lane A comparison. Title idea: 'Wegovy Pill vs Wegovy Shot: What's the Difference?' Cover how each is taken, trial weight loss for each, and that OCTANE was retrospective telehealth data and doesn't show the pill beats staying on injections. Say: 'don't switch, stop or change your current medicines on your own'.
keywords: is the wegovy pill as effective
candidates.why_now: Men's Journal (Oct 20) and Yahoo (Oct 20) coverage, the France launch (Oct 21), and the Medicare Bridge covers the pill. Our earlier pill vs shot long-form got 9, so use a pure search-phrase title or keep it Short-only.

evidence.signal: Switching to oral semaglutide linked to 4.1% weight loss at 3 months (OCTANE, retrospective)

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the kidneys in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease and obesity: new real-world study (Diabet Med, Oct 19), FLOW safety results by kidney-disease severity (Kidney Int, Oct 20), and a biomarker study predicting greater kidney benefit
candidates.angle: Single-drug body-effect question (median about 65). Title idea: 'Tirzepatide and Your Kidneys: What New Data Show'. FLOW is semaglutide in type 2 diabetes with chronic kidney disease: name each drug next to its own data and keep the observational wording.
candidates.why_now: Three kidney papers within 48 hours and little creator coverage. Fits the benefits-beyond-weight pillar.

evidence.signal: Real-world metabolic and kidney outcomes on tirzepatide in chronic kidney disease, type 2 diabetes and obesity
Semaglutide safety by chronic kidney disease severity in FLOW

candidates.topic: REJECT: 'Retatrutide reconstitution technical guide' (Apopka Voice, Oct 20)
candidates.angle: Do not cover. It's a preparation how-to for an unapproved, gray-market drug, which breaks the never-cover list. Any retatrutide safety content should go through the CBS 'what's confirmed' Lane B piece instead.
candidates.why_now: Reconstitution content is spreading alongside gray-market demand. Listed so other agents don't pick it up.

evidence.signal: Technical guide to reconstituting retatrutide vials
